title: Give screen recording stop more than five seconds to mux
head: 2477ae0e8472
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Second stop during longer grace wait can concurrently finalize the same recording
leads.consequence: If two stop invocations enter while gpu-screen-recorder is still draining, both signal it and wait without a lock; once it exits both can run ffmpeg on the same MP4, race the processed/preview paths, post duplicate saved notifications, and one can read an empty RECORDING_FILE after the other removed it. An unrelated open PR #11520 adds a cleanly merging stop lock, but it is not in this head. This is a corroboration of the brief's existing F2, not a newly introduced parsing defect.
leads.triage: corroborates_F2; #11520 flock guard verified from diff

leads.summary: On timeout the bar refreshes before SIGKILL, leaving a stale active stop button
leads.consequence: If the recorder survives the configured grace period, the refresh probes it while it is still alive and marks the bar active, then SIGKILL runs with no later refresh. Once the process is gone, another bar click invokes --stop-recording and exits 1 without refreshing. The increase from 5 to 30 seconds means this stale indicator occurs later, not on successful saves. Open PR #12471 directly addresses the ordering and merges cleanly with this head.
leads.triage: verified_out_of_scope; pre-existing indicator refresh order; open #12471 addresses it

leads.summary: Open #13362 retains a five-second stop bound for both recorder backends and conflicts with this PR's new bound
leads.consequence: #13362 changes stop detection/signaling to a pidfd-based helper and adds a wf-recorder fallback, but its loop still uses count < 50. The exact stop loop conflicts against this head, so automatic integration cannot preserve the 30-second feature. If a resolution takes #13362's loop verbatim, recordings on both backends again get SIGKILL after about five seconds; a correct combined loop needs its helper predicate with this PR's validated max. This is an open-PR merge lead, not a defect observed on pinned #12559 alone.
leads.triage: verified_factual; #13362 keeps count < 50 in rewritten loop (diff lines 589-590)

leads.summary: Open #10397 replaces the bounded signal-and-poll stop with an unbounded IPC stop
leads.consequence: #10397's planned gsr-cli stop call is a different stop protocol with no local timeout or SIGKILL escalation. GPU Screen Recorder 6.1.3 gsr-cli disables its reply timeout for stop; if the recorder is SIGSTOPed or hangs in mux, that alternative blocks until progress resumes. Its stop block conflicts with this head. The two designs need explicit reconciliation rather than assuming this PR's 30-second bound also applies after #10397 merges. This is a cross-PR conditional, not current-head behaviour.
leads.triage: verified_factual_partial; #10397 gsr-cli stop replaces SIGINT/poll; unbounded-stop consequence not published

leads.summary: Existing screen recording test passes even when the new timeout is ignored
leads.consequence: The kept test stubs pgrep to always exit 1 and invokes the changed script only for starting, so it never tests stop waiting. A disposable mutant replacing local max=$((timeout_s * 10)) with max=50 passed all 26 assertions. Thus a regression to the former five-second bound can ship with a green test; add stop fixtures for default, 010, 0, 601 and six-digit values, plus force-kill behavior.
leads.triage: not_published; test coverage gap consistent with earlier scope note; mutant evidence Sol-only

leads.summary: User-facing recording instructions still omit the new grace-period setting
leads.consequence: The new # Env: header in the binary fixes the earlier header-only documentation complaint, but neither the recording manual's options nor the FAQ's uwsm env.d example mentions OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_STOP_TIMEOUT. People tuning stop after experiencing truncation will not find the knob in the feature guide. A short manual example should clarify that a valid five-digit value over 600 clamps to 600, whereas a six-digit string reverts to 30.
leads.triage: dropped; siblings also absent from manual; header matches pattern

limits: No real GPU, desktop, recorder, FFmpeg mux or SIGSTOP runtime was exercised. comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to [the earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12559#issuecomment-5826980911) and [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12559#issuecomment-5827009715), checked at head `2477ae0`.

**Outcome:** the timeout parsing issue, the "Closes #12469" scope note and the documentation note are resolved. The concurrent second stop is still present, and the author has deferred it to a separate change. One newly found edge remains in the parsing: timeout values written with non-ASCII digits abort the stop in some glibc UTF-8 locales such as `en_US.UTF-8`.

| Earlier finding | Status on `2477ae0` |
|---|---|
| Leading-zero and very large timeout values bypass the fallback | Resolved |
| A second stop during the longer wait runs a concurrent finalize | Still present (deferred by the author) |
| Scope of "Closes #12469" | Resolved: the description now says "Mitigates #12469", and GitHub lists no closing-issue reference |
| Documentation of `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_STOP_TIMEOUT` | Resolved in the script's `# Env:` header. The uwsm `env.d` part was not adopted, which matches `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_USE_PORTAL` and `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_DEBUG` next to it in the header; neither is documented there |

### Timeout parsing

**Verified:** every value from the earlier table now either parses as decimal or falls back to 30 s, and stays within 1 to 600 s. The recorder stub keeps running after SIGINT, so each wait below is the loop bound (loop iterations × 0.1 s, not wall-clock time):

| `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_STOP_TIMEOUT` | `db9bc49` (earlier review) | `2477ae0` |
|---|---|---|
| `010` | 8 s (octal) | 10 s |
| `08`, `09` | exit 1, `value too great for base`, no finalize | 8 s, 9 s, then the force-kill toast, exit 0 |
| `0600` | 384 s (octal) | 600 s |
| `1000000000000000000` | immediate SIGKILL (overflow) | 30 s (fallback) |
| `1000`, `99999` | no upper cap (the stub recorder exited at its 700 s safety limit first) | 600 s (clamp) |

The earlier Verified results still hold on this head:
- A recorder that needs 8 s is saved at about 8.0 s, while base force-kills it at about 5.3 s (real-time runs).
- A recorder that exits promptly adds no wait.
- Non-numeric ASCII values fall back to 30 s.
- The saved and force-killed paths both exit 0.

The keybinding, menu, bar indicator and webcam wrapper all reach the same stop branch, so they get the same exit status and toasts. For ASCII input, results were identical in the `C`, `C.UTF-8` and `en_US.UTF-8` locales.

**Documentation note:** the header's "oversized digit strings" could say "more than five digits", because `99999` is clamped to 600 s while `100000` falls back to 30 s. The description's Test section says the parsing "rejects octal/`08`/`09`", but those values are now accepted and read as decimal.

### Non-ASCII digits pass the check and abort the stop (newly found)

In a glibc UTF-8 locale such as `en_US.UTF-8`, a `[0-9]` range inside Bash `=~` follows the locale's collation order, so it also matches many non-ASCII digits. A full scan of non-ASCII code points found 1,040 matches, among them fullwidth `３` and Arabic-Indic `٣`. `C` and `C.UTF-8` gave none. Such a value passes the check, and `$((10#$timeout_s))` then fails:

```text
LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8  OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_STOP_TIMEOUT=３０  (stubbed recorder)
  SIGINT sent
  line 233: 10#: invalid integer constant
  exit 1: no wait, no indicator refresh, no finalize, no toast, recording state file left behind
```

The same class of failure was already present in `db9bc49` (`^[0-9]+$`), and the earlier review's own suggested sketch kept the same `[0-9]` range.

**Impact:** only a value written with non-ASCII digits (for example, typed with a CJK input method) triggers it. Every stop then skips post-processing and the toast, and ALT+PRINT falls through to the capture menu. The recorder has already received SIGINT, so a real gpu-screen-recorder probably still writes its file. That part was not tested.

**Suggested change:** use `^[[:digit:]]{1,5}$` or `^[0123456789]{1,5}$`. In a separate scan of the same code points, neither matched any non-ASCII character, and both still accept every value from `0` to `99999`.

### Second stop during the wait (still present)

The stop path after the parsing block is unchanged. On this head, with stubs, the recorder needed 8 s and a second stop started 1 s after the first. Both stops then finalized the same recording: two `ffmpeg` writers overlapped on the same `*-processed.mp4`, one `mv` failed, and two "Screen recording saved" toasts appeared. The window now lasts up to the configured timeout (at most 600 s), but only while the recorder is still running. A second SIGINT does not affect gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.3 itself, because its handler only clears the running flag.

**Impact:** the same as in the earlier review: pressing stop again during a slow shutdown leads to duplicate processing and duplicate toasts.

**Suggested change:** a separate change, as the author proposes, is a reasonable scope. Open #11520 already adds a non-blocking `flock` guard to the stop path, so the follow-up could build on it or be coordinated with it.

**Related open PRs:** #13362 and #10397 also rewrite this stop loop. #13362 replaces the `pgrep` check with its own process helper but keeps `count < 50`. Resolving the conflict needs this PR's `max` together with that helper, or the 5 s bound returns. #10397 stops the recorder with `gsr-cli ... stop` instead of SIGINT and polling, so this timeout would not apply there.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `2477ae0` against the previously reviewed `db9bc49` and the base, covering the stop callers and gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.3 source. The stop path was exercised in isolated sandboxes on all three revisions. `pgrep`, `pkill`, `ffmpeg` and the notification helpers were stubbed, and so was `sleep` in the parsing matrix. Runs used Bash 5.3 and glibc 2.44 in the `C`, `C.UTF-8` and `en_US.UTF-8` locales, and the parsing table's waits are loop-bound counts, not wall-clock measurements. No real recorder, GPU, display or ffmpeg was used, and the repository test suite was not run. Statements about #11520, #13362 and #10397 come from reading their diffs; none of them was merged or run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical follow-up review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
